result_summary:
Now I understand the request: enable the runtime end-user Assistant by authoring the Business Area it needs to answer questions (a Business Area published with the right roles is what makes the Assistant queryable). Let me delegate this to the business-area-designer.The Business Area file is confirmed written correctly, and no other `assistant.json`/config file exists in the project — the "enable" is a property of the Business Area itself (`VISIBILITY: "published"` + `ACCESS.ALLOW_ROLES`), which is now set. That's the only project-level artifact for this feature that agents author; a draft area is never served, and a published one with granted roles is what makes the Assistant queryable.

## Summary

**Enabled the runtime Assistant** by authoring the Business Area it needs — created:
- `Metadata_Model/business_areas/fam_asset_management.json`

**What it covers:** all 16 core Fixed Asset Management tables (Asset Register as the anchor, joined to Category/Branch/Location/Department/Employee masters, Companies-Act & Income-Tax depreciation rate masters, Physical Verification + lines, Warranty/AMC coverage, and lifecycle events — Installation/Transfer/Disposal), with per-table and per-column descriptions, real join conditions (all grounded against the live schema), domain `AI_INSTRUCTIONS` (status semantics, CA vs IT depreciation are separate bases, warranty/AMC expiry logic, discrepancy meaning), and 6 example questions.

**Access:** `VISIBILITY: "published"` (served, not draft) and `ACCESS.ALLOW_ROLES: ["member"]` — matching the app's own default runtime role in `application.json`, so any signed-in user of the app can now ask the Assistant questions about assets, depreciation, custody, warranty/AMC, and verification findings.

No FRS update was needed — this is an Assistant/BI configuration, not a change to the app's functional screens.
